reference.title: AJCC 8th edition bone staging site tables
reference.intro: AJCC 8th edition Chapter 38 uses three separate pT tables based on anatomical site. Prognostic stage groups (IA–IVB) are defined ONLY for appendicular skeleton, trunk, skull, and facial bones.

groups.heading: Appendicular skeleton, trunk, skull, and facial bones
points: pT1: <= 80 mm (8 cm) in greatest dimension; pT2: > 80 mm; pT3: discontinuous tumours (skip metastases) in the primary bone site.
Stage groups (Checks only): IA (T1 G1), IB (T2–T3 G1), IIA (T1 G2–G3), IIB (T2 G2–G3), III (T3 G2–G3), IVA (M1a lung only, N0), IVB (any N1 or M1b non-lung).

groups.heading: Pelvis (four pelvic segments: iliac wing, acetabulum, pubic rami/ischium, sacrum)
points: pT1: 1 segment without extraosseous extension (a <= 80 mm, b > 80 mm).
pT2: 1 segment with extraosseous extension OR 2 segments without extraosseous extension (a <= 80 mm, b > 80 mm).
pT3: 2 segments with extraosseous extension (a <= 80 mm, b > 80 mm).
pT4a: involves sacroiliac joint and extends medial to sacral neuroforamen; pT4b: encasement of external iliac vessels or gross tumour thrombus in major pelvic vessels. No AJCC 8th stage groups.

groups.heading: Spine (five vertebral segments: right/left pedicles, right/left body halves, posterior element)
points: pT1: confined to 1 or 2 adjacent vertebral segments; pT2: 3 adjacent segments; pT3: >= 4 adjacent or any nonadjacent segments.
pT4a: extension into the spinal canal; pT4b: gross vascular invasion or tumour thrombus in the great vessels. No AJCC 8th stage groups.

reference.note: Criteria follow AJCC 8th edition Chapter 38 and CAP Bone 4.2.0.0. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

reference.title: Cortical destruction, marrow permeation and soft tissue extension
reference.intro: Assessing bone permeation, cortical integrity, and extraosseous soft tissue extension is essential both for malignancy diagnosis (especially cartilaginous lesions) and for pelvic pT2/pT3 staging and margin assessment.

groups.heading: Marrow permeation and entrapment of host lamellar bone
points: In hyaline cartilage neoplasms, permeation of medullary marrow spaces with complete encirclement (entrapment) of pre-existing host lamellar bone trabeculae separates ACT / chondrosarcoma from benign enchondroma.
Similarly, permeation of native lamellar bone separates low-grade central osteosarcoma from fibrous dysplasia.

groups.heading: Endosteal scalloping vs cortical destruction and soft tissue extension
points: Deep endosteal scalloping (> 2/3 of cortical thickness) favours ACT/chondrosarcoma over enchondroma.
Full-thickness cortical breakthrough with extraosseous soft tissue extension directly upstages pelvic bone sarcomas (pT1 -> pT2/pT3) and defines the closest soft tissue surgical margin.

groups.heading: Surface lesions without medullary invasion
points: Parosteal osteosarcoma, periosteal osteosarcoma, high-grade surface osteosarcoma and periosteal chondrosarcoma arise on the cortical surface.
Document whether the underlying cortex is breached and whether medullary canal invasion is present (seen in ~25% of parosteal osteosarcomas; does not by itself signify dedifferentiation).

reference.note: Criteria follow WHO 5th edition (2020) and CAP Bone 4.2.0.0. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

reference.title: Bone tumour types (WHO 5th edition)
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition (2020) and CAP Bone 4.2.0.0 integrate morphology with defining molecular alterations (MDM2, IDH1/2, EWSR1/CIC/BCOR, H3F3A G34W, TBXT/brachyury, SMARCB1).
reference.noteTop: Always correlate bone tumour histopathology with plain radiographs and MRI (location, matrix, cortical destruction, soft tissue mass) before finalising the diagnosis.

groups.heading: High-grade osteosarcomas (conventional, telangiectatic, small cell)
points: Conventional osteosarcoma (G3): direct production of irregular lace-like or trabecular neoplastic osteoid by markedly atypical malignant cells; subtyped as osteoblastic, chondroblastic or fibroblastic.
Small cell osteosarcoma: sheets of small round cells with focal malignant osteoid; negative for EWSR1::FLI1.
Telangiectatic osteosarcoma: blood-filled aneurysmal spaces lined by septa containing high-grade sarcomatous cells and fine osteoid.

images.caption: Conventional high-grade osteosarcoma: markedly pleomorphic malignant mesenchymal cells directly producing irregular lace-like eosinophilic neoplastic osteoid (H&E).
Small cell osteosarcoma: sheets of uniform small round blue cells accompanied by delicate lace-like malignant osteoid; lacks EWSR1 rearrangement (H&E).

groups.heading: Low-grade osteosarcomas (parosteal, low-grade central) and osteoblastoma
points: Parosteal and low-grade central osteosarcoma (G1): parallel/anastomosing woven bone trabeculae in a bland fibroblastic spindle cell stroma; MDM2 amplification (12q13–15) distinguishes them from fibrous dysplasia and osteoblastoma.
Look closely for high-grade transformation (dedifferentiation), which upgrades the tumour to G3.
Osteoblastoma: benign/locally aggressive (not staged); well-circumscribed anastomosing woven bone rimmed by plump osteoblasts with FOS/FOSB rearrangements.

images.caption: Parosteal osteosarcoma: parallel ("streamer-like") woven and lamellar bone trabeculae separated by a bland, low-grade fibroblastic spindle cell stroma (MDM2 amplified) (H&E).
Osteoblastoma: anastomosing woven bone trabeculae rimmed by plump benign osteoblasts within a loose fibrovascular stroma; lacks permeation of native bone (H&E).

groups.heading: Chondrosarcoma (conventional, dedifferentiated, mesenchymal, clear cell)
points: Conventional chondrosarcoma / ACT: hyaline cartilage lobules permeating host lamellar bone trabeculae (IDH1/IDH2 mutations in ~50% of central tumours).
Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma (G3): abrupt bimorphic interface between low-grade cartilage and a high-grade non-cartilaginous sarcoma (UPS, osteosarcoma or fibrosarcoma-like).
Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma (G3): biphasic sheets of small round cells with islands of hyaline cartilage and staghorn vessels (HEY1::NCOA2 fusion).

images.caption: Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma: abrupt transition from well-differentiated hyaline cartilage (bottom right) to a high-grade pleomorphic non-cartilaginous sarcoma (upper left) (H&E).
Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma: biphasic tumour with sheets of undifferentiated small round blue cells sharply juxtaposed against islands of hyaline cartilage (HEY1::NCOA2) (H&E).

groups.heading: Undifferentiated small round cell sarcomas (Ewing, CIC, BCOR, EWSR1::non-ETS)
points: Ewing sarcoma (G3): uniform small round cells with crisp diffuse membranous CD99, nuclear NKX2.2 and FET::ETS fusion (most commonly EWSR1::FLI1).
WHO 5th edition separates CIC-rearranged sarcoma, BCOR-altered sarcoma and EWSR1::non-ETS round cell sarcoma as distinct entities.

images.caption: Ewing sarcoma: uniform sheets of small round cells with scant pale cytoplasm and finely stippled chromatin; diffuse membranous CD99 and NKX2.2 positive (H&E).

groups.heading: Notochordal tumours (conventional, poorly differentiated and dedifferentiated chordoma)
points: Conventional chordoma: midline axial skeleton (sacrum, clivus, mobile spine); cords of vacuolated physaliphorous cells in myxoid stroma; positive for brachyury (TBXT), pan-CK, EMA and S100.
Poorly differentiated chordoma: sheets of epithelioid/rhabdoid cells with brachyury positivity and characteristic loss of SMARCB1 (INI1).

images.caption: Conventional chordoma: cords and nests of epithelioid cells with multivacuolated bubbly cytoplasm (physaliphorous cells) in abundant basophilic myxoid stroma; brachyury positive (H&E).

groups.heading: Giant cell tumour of bone (GCTB) and malignant GCTB
points: GCTB (not staged as sarcoma): epiphyseal-metaphyseal lesion with evenly spaced osteoclast-like giant cells and mononuclear stromal cells carrying H3F3A (H3-3A) p.Gly34Trp (G34W) mutation.
Malignant GCTB (primary or secondary): high-grade sarcoma juxtaposed with typical GCTB or arising at a prior GCTB site.

images.caption: Giant cell tumour of bone: uniformly distributed large osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells admixed with round-to-oval mononuclear stromal cells (H3F3A G34W positive) (H&E).

links.label: ExpertPath: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone

groups.heading: Adamantinoma of long bones
points: Classic diaphyseal tibial lesion: islands and cords of basaloid/squamoid/tubular epithelial cells (pan-CK and p63 positive) in an osteofibrous stroma.
Osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma has smaller isolated epithelial strands; dedifferentiated adamantinoma contains a high-grade sarcomatous component.

images.caption: Adamantinoma of long bones: nests and cords of basaloid/epithelial tumour cells with peripheral palisading embedded in a bland osteofibrous stroma; CK positive (H&E).

groups.heading: Vascular and other primary bone sarcomas
points: Epithelioid haemangioma (not staged) vs epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (WWTR1::CAMTA1 or YAP1::TFE3) vs angiosarcoma of bone (CD31/ERG positive, marked atypia and vasoformative/solid sheets).

Primary leiomyosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma and undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) of bone are diagnoses of exclusion requiring sampling to rule out dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma or osteosarcoma.

fields.label: Histologic grade (AJCC 8th / CAP 4.2.0.0)
fields.help: AJCC 8th groups G1 as low grade and G2–G3 as high grade. Conventional, telangiectatic, small cell, high-grade surface and dedifferentiated sarcomas and Ewing sarcoma are G3 (high grade); parosteal and low-grade central osteosarcoma are G1 (unless high-grade transformation).

reference.title: Histologic grading of bone sarcomas (AJCC 8th / WHO 5th)
reference.intro: AJCC 8th edition uses a 3-tier system (G1 = low grade; G2 and G3 = high grade for stage grouping). Grade is assigned by histologic type for most bone sarcomas and by 3-tier morphology for conventional chondrosarcoma.

groups.heading: G1: Well differentiated, low grade
points: Grade 1 chondrosarcoma / atypical cartilaginous tumour (ACT): low-to-moderate cellularity, small uniform hyperchromatic nuclei, occasional binucleation, abundant hyaline matrix, no mitoses or necrosis.
Grade-by-definition G1 osteosarcomas: parosteal osteosarcoma and low-grade central osteosarcoma (without high-grade transformation).

images.caption: Parosteal osteosarcoma: parallel ("streamer-like") woven and lamellar bone trabeculae separated by a bland, low-grade fibroblastic spindle cell stroma (MDM2 amplified) (H&E).

groups.heading: G2: Moderately differentiated, high grade (for AJCC staging)
points: Grade 2 chondrosarcoma: increased cellularity, larger plump vesicular/hyperchromatic nuclei with visible nucleoli, frequent binucleation, myxoid matrix change, rare mitoses (< 2 per 10 HPF), and focal necrosis.
Periosteal osteosarcoma is classically intermediate grade (G2). Note: AJCC 8th edition groups G2 with G3 as high grade for appendicular stage grouping (IIA/IIB/III).

groups.heading: G3: Poorly differentiated, high grade
points: Grade 3 chondrosarcoma: high cellularity, marked nuclear pleomorphism, spindle-cell peripheral zones, brisk mitotic activity (>= 2 per 10 HPF), extensive myxoid change and necrosis.

Grade-by-definition G3 bone sarcomas: conventional, telangiectatic, small cell and high-grade surface osteosarcoma; dedifferentiated and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma; Ewing, CIC and BCOR sarcomas; poorly differentiated/dedifferentiated chordoma; angiosarcoma; UPS.

images.caption: Conventional high-grade osteosarcoma: markedly pleomorphic malignant mesenchymal cells directly producing irregular lace-like eosinophilic neoplastic osteoid (H&E).
Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma: abrupt transition from well-differentiated hyaline cartilage (bottom right) to a high-grade pleomorphic non-cartilaginous sarcoma (upper left) (H&E).

reference.title: Neoadjuvant treatment effect in bone sarcomas (CAP 4.2.0.0 / Huvos)
reference.intro: Post-neoadjuvant histological response is one of the strongest independent prognostic factors in conventional osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma. Sample a full representative slab across the greatest tumour plane and map blocks to a gross photograph.

groups.heading: Good histological response (>= 90% necrosis / <= 10% viable tumour)
points: CAP Bone 4.2.0.0 expresses response as % treatment-related necrosis (= 100% minus % viable tumour); QMH records % viable tumour.
In osteosarcoma, >= 90% necrosis (<= 10% viable tumour; Huvos grade III–IV) predicts significantly improved event-free and overall survival.

groups.heading: Poor histological response (< 90% necrosis / > 10% viable tumour)
points: Sheets or confluent nests of viable pleomorphic tumour cells with intact nuclear detail and mitotic figures remaining across > 10% of the mapped tumour area.
Record the estimated percentage across the entire mapped cross-section, not from a single block.

groups.heading: Recognising treatment-related change vs viable tumour
points: Non-viable tumour: coagulative/geographic necrosis, acellular/hyalinised osteoid or chondroid matrix with empty lacunae, loose fibrous replacement, haemorrhage, haemosiderin and foamy histiocytes.
Residual acellular osteoid without viable malignant cells counts as non-viable (necrotic/treated) tumour.

reference.note: No openly licensed bone sarcoma post-chemotherapy histology photograph was included; criteria follow CAP Bone 4.2.0.0 and Huvos grading. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

fields.label: Viable tumour (%)
fields.help: QMH records % viable tumour (CAP Bone 4.2.0.0 expresses treatment-related necrosis as 100% minus viable %; >= 90% necrosis / <= 10% viable tumour is a good histological response in osteosarcoma).
